title: Field Ops midday bug-hunt digest — May 03 2027
content:
Context: quick mid-day sync from Field Ops / Install crew doing a targeted bug-hunt against three live installs that showed flakey performance during heavy inference loads. Note: this is a working log — action items and owners at the bottom.

High-level summary:
- Focus: 3 active customer installs (Aldora Analytics, BlueRidge Health, Zephyr Labs) experiencing intermittent tokenization stalls and very high p95 tail latency under burst traffic.
- Hypothesis so far: combination of packet fragmentation (MTU + iptables NAT) and KV cache thrashing on nodes with mixed GPU/CPU scheduling.
- Short-term mitigations deployed where possible; longer-term fixes tracked in JIRA-OPS-1842 and the network runbook update.

Detailed notes:
1) Aldora Analytics (on-prem private cluster, 10 nodes — mixed GPU types)
   - Symptom: 10–30s stalls on generate requests between tokens 32–64, correlated with sudden CPU spikes on control-plane sidecar (model-proxy).
   - Observations:
     * Network traces show ICMP fragmentation events and repeated retransmits at ~MTU 1500 boundaries.
     * iptables MASQUERADE rules were autogenerated by an older kube-proxy config; some packets take an unexpected path via host NIC causing extra MTU overhead.
     * KV cache eviction spikes coincide with the stalls; cache hit-rate drops from 96% to 33% during incidents.
   - Immediate fixes tried:
     * Adjusted host MTU to 9000 on GPU nodes (Leah) — reduced fragmentation in synthetic tests but needs validation under customer traffic.
     * Pinned model-proxy sidecar CPU limit from 200m -> 800m to prevent preemption during short bursts (Jinwoo). Observed fewer stalls in Canary harness.
   - Remaining risks: persistent cache thrash if sequence length distribution varies; planning a cache warm-up preflight for high-variance workloads.

2) BlueRidge Health (VPC private deployment in customer cloud account)
   - Symptom: persistent TLS handshake slowdowns and occasional certificate validation errors during autoscaling events. Affected generated tokens sometimes truncated.
   - Observations:
     * Cloud metadata service rate-limiting during scale-out caused delays in our startup hook that fetches certs from customer KMS proxy.
     * Some transient DNS failures observed — dig shows intermittent NXDOMAIN for internal cert-rotater service.
   - Mitigations applied:
     * Introduced exponential backoff and jitter in cert fetch logic (rolled a hotfix PR to edge-agent, PR#421).
     * Added local cert cache with TTL of 10m to reduce immediate dependency on metadata/KMS during burst scale-outs.
   - Next steps: coordinate with customer infra to ensure metadata quotas are sufficient and add a KMS-side async refresh path.

3) Zephyr Labs (air-gapped onprem; heavy short-lived bursts from model-eval jobs)
   - Symptom: intermittent NVMe IO stalls causing kubelet to mark pods NotReady briefly; scheduler then placed requests on warmer but lower-throughput nodes. P95 latency spikes.
   - Observations:
     * iostat shows periodic write amplification during model load and checkpoint writes.
     * Our model bundles were uncompressed in this install which increased IO footprint on cold starts.
   - Mitigations:
     * Switched to compressed model bundles in the deploy manifest and enabled streaming load path to reduce spike IO (Oscar).
     * Added a QoS policy for provisioning ephemeral NVMe space for model loads (needs infra approval).

Cross-cutting technical signals and discoveries:
- KV cache behavior: current default eviction policy (approx-LRU tuned for hosted) doesn't map well to customer onprem with high sequence-length variance. Need a knob for stronger prefix caching and a prefetch/warmup API.
- Networking: MTU mismatches and NAT-ed paths repeatedly surface in onprem sites with legacy routing. Add MTU sanity-check to install preflight and a post-install network verification test.
- Observability gaps: customers reported stalls as "random slowdowns" with no easy way to reason about whether cause is network, IO, or cache. We should add a triage probe that collects: token timing histogram, kv-cache hit-rate, immediate host MTU, and recent cert fetch latencies.
- Rolling fallback behavior worked in all three cases: when a node became unhealthy we failed over to lower-power dedicated nodes (automated), keeping customer UX mostly intact — shoutout to SRE preflight work.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Add MTU preflight check to installer and docs (Leah) — ETA: 2027-05-10 (PR for runbook in confluence).
- Expose KV-cache warmup API and a config toggle for stronger prefix retention (Eng-serving-runtime) — Owner: Jinwoo Park, ETA: 2027-05-17.
- Hotfix for cert fetch backoff landed; monitor BlueRidge for 72h and report (Maya) — ETA: 2027-05-06.
- Implement compressed model-bundle deploy option in private-deploy manifests and update installer default (Oscar) — ETA: 2027-05-12.
- Create a combined triage probe (token-timing + cache + MTU + cert latency) and add to console telemetry for Private nodes (Observability) — Owner: Priya Singh (observability), ETA: 2027-05-24.
- Customer follow-ups: schedule alignment calls with Aldora infra (networking team) and BlueRidge ops (KMS quotas) — Owners: Solutions Eng (Leah) and Customer Success (Ethan), by 2027-05-07.

Notes to self / items to capture in runbook:
- When an onprem install is mixed GPU-arch, default scheduling should bias identical-arch pods together to avoid heterogeneous IO profiles on the same host.
- Add explicit guidance for enabling jumbo frames as optional step during preflight; provide fallback if switching MTU isn't possible (tunnel-based MTU compensation).
- Document temporary cache_limit increase for installs with >2x sequence length variance observed in telemetry.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Is the NVMe write amplification at Zephyr a function of underlying filesystem (XFS vs ext4) or our write pattern? Need a controlled repro with fio (Oscar).
- For hosted-to-private parity: how much of the cache policy tuning do we want as install-time defaults vs operator-tunable?

Quick decisions made during session:
- We will not change default MTU for existing installs without customer consent. All MTU changes require preflight sign-off.
- We will prioritize the cert-fetch backoff hotfix and the KV-cache warmup API over larger scheduling changes this sprint.

Summary / next sync:
- Re-check metrics and customer reports after 72h observation window for BlueRidge and Aldora.
- Standup tomorrow 09:30 PT to go over progress on MTU preflight PR and KV-cache API design.

Raw dump of CLI commands run in troubleshooting (for reference):
- tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/aldora-frag.pcap host 10.23.4.8 and port 443
- ip link set dev ens3 mtu 9000 (test only)
- curl -v --resolve cert-rotater.internal:443:10.0.1.5 https://cert-rotater.internal:443/health | ts
- iostat -x 1 10 /dev/nvme0n1

If you were here: please add any notes below this line (timestamped).

-- end of digest --
